title: Fresh-seed review (9, 10, 11) of c33's phoretic swim-then-divide composites: Janus composites form from the random gas and divide to generation 6-9 with both daughters capped on every seed; a composite that travels >= 3 diameters merger-free and then divides into two capped daughters appears on 2 of 3 seeds (0/38, 1/36, 3/34 dividing parents), a rare minority as claimed
summary: Re-ran the claimed world unchanged on seed 9 with labkit (1600 frames, t=800; rerun/seed9) and with the claim's screen.py on seeds 9, 10 and 11 (t=800), then the claim's lineage.py (merge-aware, travel restarted at every merge). All three start from a uniform random A/B/food gas and form Janus composites (red A body, blue B cap; s9.png-s11.png). Persistent splits (40-frame hold): 38, 36, 34; max generation 7, 9, 6; both daughters carry B in 38/38, 33/36, 32/34. Parents that travelled >= 3 cluster diameters since their birth or last merge before splitting: seed 9 0 of 38 (max 2.2), seed 10 1 of 36 (track 147: 4.1 diameters, 98 -> 59 + 39, B 0.20/0.21), seed 11 3 of 34 (tracks 258: 4.5, 302: 4.0, 191: 3.4 diameters; 191 -> 28 + 22 with B 0.32/0.41, 302 -> 70 + 36 with B 0.23/0.14, 258 leaves one daughter without B). labkit on seed 9: merge/split 1.23 (reticulate), max 10.4 labkit body lengths for any track.

verdicts.limitation: Minority capability: 4 of 108 dividing parents on my seeds travel >= 3 diameters first (0, 1, 3 per seed), in line with the claim's 3 of 132. Diameters are cluster diameters 1.8 sqrt(n/pi) of round composites (>= sqrt(area)). The genealogy is reticulate (labkit merge/split 1.23 on seed 9). I did not re-run the reciprocal twin. lineage.py crashes on seed 10 because a float32 position equals L exactly (cKDTree periodic box); I wrapped positions mod L before running it (no other change).
